Name: Natural Irrigation Realistic Water Proximity and Crop Growth
Author: ZeroXPatch
TagLine: Natural Irrigation Realistic Water Proximity and Crop Growth
Description:
🐻Natural Irrigation – Realistic Water Proximity & Crop Growth🐸

Support 13 languages

Safe to uninstall anytime. Removing it just disables the features.

This mod is available for download here on CurseForge. For bug reports, feature requests, or community discussions, please visit our official Nexus Mods page:
https://www.nexusmods.com/profile/ZeroXPatch/mods?sortBy=endorsements

Crops planted right next to water should benefit from it – not behave the same as a lonely patch in the middle of a field.

Natural Irrigation makes water proximity actually matter: soil near rivers, ponds, and other water tiles starts the day hydrated,

and crops growing in the “extra moist” zone have a chance to grow a little faster.

Everything is configurable and designed to feel like a natural extension of vanilla gameplay, not a cheat.






 
What the mod does

🌊 Water-fed soil based on distance to water

Each morning, the mod looks at your tilled soil and checks how close it is to natural water sources:

Rivers
Ponds
Any tile on the map marked as “Water”
If a tile is within the water search radius (configurable), that soil starts the day watered, as if it stayed moist overnight thanks to nearby water.


Default radius: 4 tiles
Can be lowered, raised, or disabled entirely (radius 0)
Mechanically this is still Stardew’s watering system, but the reason your soil is wet is now tied to the landscape instead of just tools and sprinklers.

 
💧 Moisture tiers & growth bonuses

Not all irrigated soil is equal. Tiles very close to water are treated as extra moist:


Tiles within the High Moisture Radius (default: 1 tile from water) are considered in a high-moisture zone.
Crops growing on those tiles have a configurable chance per day to gain an extra day of growth progress:
They advance faster through their current growth phase.
Fully grown crops are not affected.
No items or stats are changed, just growth speed.
Config options:


High moisture radius – how close crops must be to water to qualify (in tiles).
Growth chance (%) – the daily chance that eligible crops get the extra growth tick.
This makes shorelines, riverbanks, and pond edges feel like genuinely valuable farming spots without being over-the-top.

 
🧪 Optional Natural Irrigation overlay (debug tool)

For players who like to understand exactly what a mod is doing, there’s an optional debug overlay:


Highlights soil that is currently benefiting from Natural Irrigation.
Shows irrigated tiles and high-moisture tiles in different tints.
The overlay is OFF by default – it won’t appear in normal play unless you enable it and toggle it on.
You can:
Allow/disallow the overlay in the config.
Set a custom toggle key (default: F8) to turn it on/off in-game.
Use it to plan farm layouts or just to satisfy your curiosity about how far the water’s influence reaches.

 
Configuration

All settings are configurable.

In-game (with GMCM)If you install Generic Mod Config Menu, you can manage everything from the title screen or pause menu:


Enable Natural Irrigation
Turn the entire effect on or off.
Water search radius
How many tiles from water still count as “naturally irrigated”.
High moisture radius
The radius where soil is considered extra moist and can get growth bonuses.
Growth chance (%)
Chance per day for crops in the high-moisture zone to gain extra growth progress.
Allow overlay
Whether the debug overlay feature is available at all (it still starts hidden).
Overlay toggle key
Which key toggles the overlay in-game (default F8).
Manual config.jsonIf you don’t use GMCM, the mod will generate a config.json after you run the game once.
You can edit it with any text editor while the game is closed.


 
Compatibility

Designed for Stardew Valley 1.6+ and SMAPI 4.x.
Works with:
All standard farm types
Most custom maps, as long as they use normal water tiles or mark water properly
Doesn’t edit vanilla assets or XNBs.
Doesn’t add new items or buff systems – it only influences soil state and crop growth logic.
Should be safe to add or remove mid-save. Tiles will simply stop or start benefiting from Natural Irrigation depending on whether the mod is installed/active.
